purpose: Source-addressed independent evidence for Alpha underwriting; no numeric underwriting or canonical judgment.

facts: Infleqtion disclosed that approximately 60% of fiscal-2025 revenue came from U.S. government customers and approximately 13% from UK government contracts.
The filing states future government revenue depends on appropriations, budget priorities and continued contract awards, creating a material concentration/execution risk.
The filing also identifies qualified-personnel availability and immigration/work-permit changes as potential development and growth constraints.

interpretation.observed: The regulatory filing independently quantifies customer concentration that the existing packet listed only as an Alpha-owned unknown.
interpretation.whyItMatters: It converts customer concentration from an unspecified unknown into source-addressed underwriting evidence and gives Alpha a concrete risk input for confidence and scenario robustness.
unknowns: Current 2026 customer concentration after Q2 growth remains to be recomputed by Alpha from current filings; this artifact does not infer a 2026 percentage.
contradictions: Rapid 2026 commercialization growth coexists with historically high government-customer concentration and funding-cycle exposure.
